title: Test-Time Learning of Causal Structure from Interventional Data
claim: Our method consistently beats the strongest baseline across diverse task settings and low-sample regimes, with large gains on target detection.
layout: 4 bar-chart panels left, 1 circular radial bar chart right; red gain annotations
description: A wide figure with two parts. On the left is a 2x2 grid of grouped bar charts. Each compares F1-score (%) of TICL (light blue) against the baseline Next (light green) on Asia, Child and Water datasets. Each panel splits into I-CPDAG discovery and intervention-target detection, separated by a dashed vertical line. Settings are named under each panel, e.g. Hard+Single+Unknown, Soft+Multiple+Unknown, limited observational samples and limited interventional samples. Dashed lines with curved arrows mark the gap, and red text gives percentage gains such as +13.7%, +58.0% and +63.0%. On the right is a circular radial bar chart for Soft+Multiple+Unknown. Its sectors cover Win95pts, Asia, Sachs, Child, Water and Alarm. The bars show relative improvement on SHD, SID, F1 (I-CPDAG) and F1 (I). The chart carries a +20.0% label and an orange reference circle.
caption: (Empirical dominance across interventional SCL tasks). \model consistently outperforms all SoTA methods on both $\mathcal{I}$-CPDAG discovery and intervention targets detection, across diverse intervention families and limited-sample regimes.
abstract: Supervised causal learning has shown promise in causal discovery, yet it often struggles with generalization across diverse interventional settings, particularly when intervention targets are unknown. To address this, we propose TICL (Test-time Interventional Causal Learning), a novel method that synergizes Test-Time Training with Joint Causal Inference. Specifically, we design a self-augmentation strategy to generate instance-specific training data at test time, effectively avoiding distribution shifts. Furthermore, by integrating joint causal inference, we developed a PC-inspired two-phase supervised learning scheme, which effectively leverages self-augmented training data while ensuring theoretical identifiability. Extensive experiments on bnlearn benchmarks demonstrate TICL's superiority in multiple aspects of causal discovery and intervention target detection.
